definition: A dry, one-seeded fruit with a papery wing, as on a maple, ash, or elm; often called a winged seed.
etymology: Botanists borrowed it into New Latin from Latin samara, meaning “elm seed.” The old Roman name settled onto a broader family of spinning, wind-borne fruits.
usage: By mid-October, the maples had begun to scatter their samaras across the path like small, tan propellers.
